subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Dunning-Kruger Effect
description: A quick win: understand The Dunning-Kruger Effect.

hook.text: A bank robber covered his face in lemon juice, believing it made him invisible to cameras.

buildup.text: Dunning and Kruger found that the least skilled people overestimate their ability the most.

discovery.text: Low competence prevents recognizing low competence. You need skill to know you lack it.

twist.text: Experts do the opposite: they underestimate themselves because they see how much they still don't know.

climax.text: Confidence peaks at the start and at mastery. The painful middle is where real learning happens.

punchline.text: Doubt is a sign you're getting smarter.

quiz.question: Why do the least skilled overestimate their abilities?
options: They lack the skill needed to recognize their incompetence
They have had too much training
